toolset: The .NET SDK 10.0.402 host (dotnet msbuild), tree on net10.0-windows / net10.0. Counts are unique findings, not log lines (see "note") and are NOT comparable with any baseline generated before 2026-10-18, nor with a Visual Studio MSBuild log - see README.md, "The warning ratchet" and "Retargeting the tree to .NET 10".
note: Maximum allowed occurrences per warning code. Regenerate with warnings.ps1 -UpdateBaseline after an intentional change and record why in notes.<CODE> and the commit message. Codes listed in "untracked" are reported under "informational" instead and never fail the gate.

notes.CA1401: 56 findings (was 57; the public GetDiskFreeSpaceEx declaration in Utilities\FileSystem\DriveUtils.cs was deleted together with the dead method that called it - CA1401 is 'P/Invokes should not be visible', so a public DllImport is the finding itself). P/Invoke declarations without AllowSetForegroundWindow-style guards; they move when the Win32 layer moves behind a platform seam.
notes.CA1416: CA1416 findings are counted as unique (file, line, code, message), never as log lines. Floor history, each step one parser run over the same build log: 196 at the net10 retarget (17 of them newly *seen* WinForms sites in MP2-Server rather than new debt - the full story is in docs/multiplatform/ROADMAP.md), 161 when MediaPortal.Utilities became the first core assembly on a portable target framework (its own sites went 35 -> 12 -> 3 -> 0: platform guards, an XDG desktop entry translating the autostart registry key, then dead code deleted along with the System.Management and System.Drawing.Common references it existed for), 147 when the Dokan binding moved out to MediaPortal.Common.Windows (14 = 13 in Dokan\Proxy.cs + 1 in DokanFileInfo.cs), 140 when the Windows impersonation service moved with it (7 = 6 in WindowsIdentityWrapper.cs spread over 5 source lines + 1 in LogonHelper.cs), 131 when the crash logger stopped needing WMI and the power handling moved out: -20 for CrashLoggerBase's Win32_LogicalDisk enumeration (now System.IO.DriveInfo) and HKLM CentralProcessor read (now guarded, with /proc/cpuinfo on Linux) at 13, SystemStateService 4, PowerEventHandler 1 and ApplicationCore's product-name registry block 1, then +11 back. Those 11 are the seam pattern's price, not new debt: MP2-Server calls WindowsSystemStateService exactly the way it already calls the three satellite Register() methods. It is flagged for that because MediaPortal.Server is built with GenerateAssemblyInfo=false, which also suppresses the [SupportedOSPlatform] attribute the SDK derives from a -windows target framework - verified: that project has no generated AssemblyInfo.cs at all, while the satellite's contains two of them. That sentence was written from a probe that turned out to be wrong, and correcting it is the useful part. An <AssemblyAttribute> item is inert while GenerateAssemblyInfo=false, because the item is consumed by the very target that property disables; and the 'zero' came from a filter that matched nothing (the [project] tag follows the warning text in an MSBuild log, and the pattern assumed it preceded it). What works is the MP2AddWindowsPlatformAttribute target in Directory.Build.targets, which writes the single attribute the SDK would have written: applied to 106 projects, none of them portable, and CA1416 went 131 -> 0 (all 107 distinct sites were in -windows projects, MP2-Server's own Application.Run and MessageBox.Show among them), findings 618 -> 487 with no other code moving by a single finding. Both relocations left the combined spine total at 180; spine.ps1 prints them as relocated, not fixed, and satellites.ps1 names the namespaces that changed owner. CA1416 is a proxy only: it cannot see a [DllImport], a Windows path inside a string, or WinForms under a -windows target framework, so the real Windows budget is combinedTotalRefs in spine-baseline.json plus the P/Invoke column.

notes.NETSDK1189: 0 findings, and the entry is deliberately left out of the floors rather than set to 0: if this code comes back it should fail as an unknown code, because it is the SDK's own complaint 'Prefer32Bit is not supported and has no effect for netcoreapp target', and its return would mean somebody put Prefer32Bit back into an executable. notes.NU1504: 1 finding: duplicated PackageReference entries in MediaPortal.Mock (System.Data.SQLite.Core listed twice).
notes.NU1510: 19 findings on 2026-10-18 (was 20; one went when MediaPortal.Mock's duplicate System.Data.SQLite.Core reference was deleted). PackageReferences the SDK now supplies implicitly: four packages over 36 projects (Microsoft.CSharp in 31, then System.Threading.Tasks.Dataflow, System.Resources.Extensions, System.Security.Permissions). The fifth used to be System.Drawing.Common in MediaPortal.Utilities and it went with that project's move to a portable target framework, which is the only way this line shrinks: the SDK can call a reference unnecessary, but only a call graph says it is also an unused one. Removing them is safe and each is a one-line deletion; they are not counted here because the number depends on which projects a given build pass re-evaluated, which packages.ps1 measures from project.assets.json instead.
notes.NU1701: 20 findings from seven packages over 33 projects on 2026-10-18, new with net10: those packages only offer .NET Framework assets and are consumed through the compatibility fallback. Six of the seven (BASS.NET, BassRegistration, MediaPortal.TagLib, OnlineVideos.Core, WorldWeatherOnlineHelper, DiscUtils) are also the packages that only ever existed on the dead MyGet feed, so none of them can be replaced until Phase 1a vendors or replaces them; SharpLibHid is on nuget.org but has no .NET Standard assets.
notes.NU1902: 0 findings as of 2026-10-18; it was 50 when the retarget landed, and this code simply did not exist on the old tree: NuGet audit is switched on for net8.0+ targets, so the net48/net6.0 legs never evaluated package advisories. The retarget turned on a detector that had been off the whole time. What actually closed it: log4net 2.0.14 -> 3.5.0 in MediaPortal.Common.csproj (104 projects inherited the single reference; GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w is only patched from 3.3.0, so no 2.x bump could have cleared it), Microsoft.Windows.Compatibility deleted from Setup\Tests which also removed the transitive System.Data.SqlClient 4.8.5, and DotNetZip deleted from LogCollector which also removed the transitive System.Drawing.Common 5.0.0 that NuGet rates Critical (NU1904, GHSA-rxg9-xrhp-64gj). packages.ps1 -FailOn Low exits 0 on the tree now, so this list is the record of a closed surface rather than an open one; NU1901/NU1904 are listed in untracked alongside 1902/1903 so that a future advisory of any severity lands in packages.ps1, where it names the package, rather than as a count of log lines.

notes.SYSLIB0011: BinaryFormatter: 12 findings -> 0, and the code is absent from the file. On .NET 8+ this is an error, not a warning, so the retarget made it impossible to keep: TvdbLib\Cache\BinaryCacheProvider.cs was deleted (its own comment said "broken at the moment -> use CacheProvider") and DiskCachedDictionary now serialises with JsonConvert *without* TypeNameHandling - that option would reintroduce exactly the deserialization gadget risk BinaryFormatter is famous for. If this code reappears, something re-enabled binary deserialization of untrusted data.
